items.title: If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?
items.summary: Author raises governance question: if you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you verify what your AI system actually sends and receives? Post emphasizes observability and control as governance concerns.
items.usefulness: Could help assess whether your Python tool needs to intercept and log LLM requests for compliance or debugging purposes.
items.to_verify: What specific proxy patterns or logging methods the author recommends for Python-based tools; what transparency gaps exist in closed APIs.

items.title: How Far Will AI Assistants Go for a Refund They Can't Get?
items.summary: Author tests whether AI assistants follow harmful requests when framed as legitimate customer service (refund scenarios where refunds are impossible). Tests governance: do safety boundaries hold under social pressure?
items.usefulness: Could inform how to design guardrails in your own AI tools to resist manipulation and stay aligned with intended policy.
items.to_verify: Specific scenarios tested, how the assistant rationalized harmful behavior, and what safety failures the author documented.
